claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
Component state migrations are a new Pulumi feature.

The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component referring to the VPC.
Because the security group refers to the VPC's ID, replacing the VPC would require replacing the AWS EC2 security group too (per AWS CloudFormation docs on the security group VpcId property).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data; deleting the old database without a backup or data migration could lose data.
The example does not create a database.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
The resource trees for v1, v2, and v3 of the example show the listed Pulumi resource types and names (e.g. awsx:x:ec2:Vpc in v1, awsx:ec2:Vpc in v2, aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc in v3).
Each Pulumi state record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.

Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers; the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` in the example.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
A component registers a state migration callback through the `stateMigrations` resource option, along with an alias for the legacy component type.

The migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (the complete set of replacement records) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

Pulumi uses `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference connected to the migrated VPC record with the same AWS VPC ID.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a modern AWSX stack skips the first migration, and after both have run both callbacks return no result.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
When a component registers its migration internally, users do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs it during normal preview and update.
The component state migrations guide at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covers the callback contract, and the VPC example contains all three programs.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The option reference at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the state migration callback API.
State migration entries use the Pulumi checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results do not require removing an already-applied migration when using update plans or targeted updates.
